items.stem: Complete the statement: The payback period is …
options: the average annual profit as a percentage of investment
the time taken for the net cash inflows from a project to repay the initial investment
the discount rate that gives zero NPV
items.answer: the time taken for the net cash inflows from a project to repay the initial investment
items.markingKey: Payback = time to recover initial outlay [1].

items.stem: Explain why a business with cash-flow problems might rely on the payback method.
items.answer: Payback focuses on how quickly cash is recovered, reducing liquidity risk and exposure to uncertain later years.

items.stem: Explain two disadvantages of the accounting rate of return.
items.answer: Ignores the time value of money; uses profit (affected by depreciation policy) rather than cash; ignores timing of returns; different definitions of investment.

items.stem: Delta Ltd is considering a new packaging line costing $455,000. Net cash inflows are expected to be: year 1 $222,500, year 2 $205,000, year 3 $153,500. Calculate the payback period in years and months.
items.answer: 2 years 2 months
items.markingKey: Cumulative cash flow reaches $27,500 still to recover at the start of year 3 [1]; $27,500/$153,500 × 12 = 2 months [1]; payback 2 years 2 months [1]

items.stem: Tamarind Ltd is considering a solar power system costing $80,000. Net cash inflows are expected to be: year 1 $26,500, year 2 $22,000, year 3 $28,500, year 4 $26,000, year 5 $28,500. Calculate the payback period in years and months.
items.answer: 3 years 1 month
items.markingKey: Cumulative cash flow reaches $3,000 still to recover at the start of year 4 [1]; $3,000/$26,000 × 12 = 1 month [1]; payback 3 years 1 month [1]

items.stem: Sunbird plc is considering a cold-storage unit costing $100,000. Net cash inflows are expected to be: year 1 $46,500, year 2 $63,000, year 3 $44,000. The company requires payback within 2 years. Calculate the payback period in years and months and advise whether the project meets the target.
items.answer: 1 year 10 months — meets the target
items.markingKey: Cumulative cash flow reaches $53,500 still to recover at the start of year 2 [1]; $53,500/$63,000 × 12 = 10 months [1]; payback 1 year 10 months [1] ; conclusion [1]

items.stem: Sunbird plc can invest $95,000 in one of two projects, each lasting 4 years with no residual value. Project P cash inflows: year 1 $40,500, year 2 $35,000, year 3 $24,500, year 4 $28,000. Project Q cash inflows: year 1 $170,500, year 2 $172,000, year 3 $197,500, year 4 $166,000. (a) Calculate the ARR of each project on average investment. (b) Explain why neither method takes account of the time value of money.
items.answer: (a) P 17.4%; Q 321.6% (b) Both treat $1 received in year 4 as equal to $1 now; they do not discount future flows.
items.markingKey: (a) Average profit [2]; average investment [1]; ARR each [1] [4] (b) [2]

items.stem: Sirocco plc can invest $335,000 in one of two projects, each lasting 4 years with no residual value. Project P cash inflows: year 1 $142,000, year 2 $99,500, year 3 $95,500, year 4 $142,500. Project Q cash inflows: year 1 $82,000, year 2 $94,500, year 3 $98,500, year 4 $110,500. (a) Calculate the payback period of each project. (b) Explain why neither method takes account of the time value of money.
items.answer: (a) P 3 years 0 months; Q 3 years 7 months (b) Both treat $1 received in year 4 as equal to $1 now; they do not discount future flows.

items.stem: Complete the statement: The accounting rate of return uses …
options: profit after depreciation rather than cash flow
only the first year's cash flow
items.answer: profit after depreciation rather than cash flow
items.markingKey: ARR = average annual profit / (average or initial) investment × 100 [1].

items.stem: Explain one advantage of ARR over payback.
items.answer: ARR considers profit over the whole life of the project and gives a percentage that can be compared with ROCE or a target return.

items.stem: Ibis plc is evaluating a fishing vessel costing $380,000 with a life of 4 years and no residual value. Depreciation is straight-line. Net cash inflows: year 1 $115,000, year 2 $141,500, year 3 $119,500, year 4 $114,000. Calculate the accounting rate of return based on the initial investment.
items.markingKey: Total profit = $490,000 − depreciation $380,000 = $110,000 [1]; average profit $27,500 [1]; initial investment $380,000 [1]; ARR = 7.2% [1]

items.stem: Vanguard Ltd has spent $11,000 on a feasibility study for a cold-storage unit costing $195,000, life 4 years, residual value $9,000. Forecast revenue: year 1 $104,000, year 2 $174,000, year 3 $110,000, year 4 $140,000; cash operating costs: $51,000, $88,000, $55,000, $50,000. Straight-line depreciation of $46,500 a year has been included in the accountant's profit forecast. Cost of capital 12%; discount factors 0.893, 0.797, 0.712, 0.636. (a) Calculate the net cash flow for each year. (b) Explain why the feasibility study cost is ignored.
items.answer: (a) $53,000, $86,000, $55,000, $99,000 (b) It is a sunk cost already incurred whatever the decision, so it is not relevant.
items.markingKey: (a) Revenue − cash costs [1]; depreciation and sunk cost excluded [1]; residual in year 4 [1] [3] (b) [2]

items.stem: Complete the statement: A project should be accepted under the NPV method if …
options: its total cash inflows exceed cost, ignoring timing
its payback is less than 5 years
its net present value is positive
items.answer: its net present value is positive

items.stem: Explain why NPV is considered superior to payback and ARR.
items.answer: It uses cash flows, considers the whole life of the project and the time value of money, and gives an absolute increase in wealth.
items.markingKey: Time value [1]; whole life/cash flows [1]; wealth measure [1] [3]

items.stem: Explain two difficulties in using NPV.
items.answer: Estimating future cash flows accurately; choosing an appropriate discount rate (cost of capital); difficult to explain to non-financial managers.

items.stem: Monarch plc is considering a bottling machine costing $395,000. Net cash inflows: year 1 $147,000, year 2 $205,500, year 3 $170,000. The cost of capital is 10%; discount factors: year 1 0.909, year 2 0.826, year 3 0.751. Calculate the net present value and state whether the project should be accepted.
items.answer: NPV $36,036 — accept (positive)

items.stem: Explain why working capital released at the end of a project is a cash inflow.
items.answer: Inventory and receivables tied up at the start are turned back into cash when the project ends.

options: the average accounting profit as a percentage of cost
the discount rate at which the net present value of a project is zero
items.answer: the discount rate at which the net present value of a project is zero

items.stem: Explain why IRR found by linear interpolation is only an approximation.
items.answer: NPV does not change linearly with the discount rate (the NPV curve is convex), so a straight-line estimate between two points differs slightly from the true rate.
items.markingKey: Non-linear relationship [1]; estimate depends on rates chosen [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage of IRR compared with NPV.
items.answer: Advantage: a percentage is easy to understand and compare with cost of capital. Disadvantage: may rank mutually exclusive projects wrongly; ignores size of project; can have multiple IRRs with unusual cash flows.

items.stem: A project has an NPV of $12,986 at 10% and -$8,322 at 18%. Estimate the internal rate of return by interpolation and state whether the project is acceptable with a cost of capital of 12%.
items.answer: IRR ≈ 14.9%; acceptable

items.stem: Osprey Ltd is evaluating a bottling machine costing $77,200 with net cash inflows year 1 $24,000, year 2 $25,500, year 3 $28,000, year 4 $32,500. Discount factors at 10%: 0.909, 0.826, 0.751, 0.683; at 18%: 0.847, 0.718, 0.609, 0.516. Calculate the NPV at each rate and estimate the IRR.

Marula plc is considering a 3D printer costing $378,000 with cash inflows year 1 $123,500, year 2 $171,000, year 3 $129,500, year 4 $99,000. Its cost of capital is 9%. Discount factors at 10%: 0.909, 0.826, 0.751, 0.683; at 20%: 0.833, 0.694, 0.579, 0.482. (a) Estimate the IRR by interpolation. (b) Explain what the IRR tells the directors about the project's risk.
items.answer: (a) 15.4% (b) It shows the maximum cost of capital the project can bear before NPV becomes negative; a small gap above the cost of capital means little margin for error.

items.stem: Complete the statement: A project should be accepted under IRR if …
options: its IRR equals the payback period
its IRR is lower than the cost of capital
its IRR is higher than the cost of capital
items.answer: its IRR is higher than the cost of capital
items.markingKey: IRR > cost of capital → positive NPV [1].

items.stem: A project has an NPV of $27,200 at 8% and -$21,900 at 14%. A student estimated the IRR as 38.8% using 8 + $27,200/($27,200 − $21,900) × 6. Explain the error and calculate the correct IRR.
items.answer: The range between the NPVs is $27,200 + $21,900 = $49,100 because one NPV is negative; IRR = 8 + $27,200/$49,100 × 6 = 11.3%.
items.markingKey: Denominator should be the total difference $49,100 [1]; method [1]; IRR 11.3% [1] [3]

items.stem: Complete the statement: Sensitivity analysis in investment appraisal shows …
options: how much a variable can change before the project's NPV becomes zero
items.answer: how much a variable can change before the project's NPV becomes zero
items.markingKey: Sensitivity = NPV / PV of the variable × 100 [1].

items.stem: Explain two limitations of sensitivity analysis.
items.answer: It changes one variable at a time while others are held constant; it does not give the probability of a change; it does not tell managers what decision to make.

items.stem: Explain why non-financial factors should be considered alongside NPV.
items.answer: Some effects (environmental impact, staff morale, reputation, legal requirements, strategic fit) are hard to quantify but can affect long-term success or the reliability of forecasts.
items.markingKey: Hard to quantify but important [1]; two examples [1] [2]

items.stem: Pinnacle Ltd can invest $275,000 in one of two projects, each lasting 4 years with no residual value. items.answer: (a) Payback favours Q; ARR favours Q. Both methods agree. Consider risk and liquidity. (b) Both treat $1 received in year 4 as equal to $1 now; they do not discount future flows.

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) Which cash flow should be EXCLUDED from an NPV calculation? (b) Complete the statement: Discounting cash flows takes account of …

items.markingKey: (a) Depreciation is non-cash; also exclude sunk costs [1]. (b) $1 today is worth more than $1 in future [1].

items.stem: Banyan Ltd appraised an automated warehouse costing $240,000 with cash inflows of year 1 $141,500, year 2 $112,500, year 3 $87,500. items.stem: A project has an NPV of $9,500 at 12% and -$21,300 at 18%. A student estimated the IRR as 7.2% using 12 + $9,500/($9,500 − $21,300) × 6. Explain the error and calculate the correct IRR.
items.answer: The range between the NPVs is $9,500 + $21,300 = $30,800 because one NPV is negative; IRR = 12 + $9,500/$30,800 × 6 = 13.9%.
items.markingKey: Denominator should be the total difference $30,800 [1]; method [1]; IRR 13.9% [1] [3]

items.stem: A project has an NPV of $28,200 at 10% and -$26,400 at 20%. A student estimated the IRR as 166.7% using 10 + $28,200/($28,200 − $26,400) × 10. Explain the error and calculate the correct IRR.
items.answer: The range between the NPVs is $28,200 + $26,400 = $54,600 because one NPV is negative; IRR = 10 + $28,200/$54,600 × 10 = 15.2%.
items.markingKey: Denominator should be the total difference $54,600 [1]; method [1]; IRR 15.2% [1] [3]

items.stem: Meridian Ltd has calculated a positive NPV of $92,000 for buying machinery from a new overseas supplier. Explain two non-financial factors the directors should consider before deciding.
items.answer: Reliability of supply, after-sales service, exchange-rate risk and quality.

items.stem: Quetzal plc plans to invest $338,000 in a solar power system producing an annual net cash inflow of $91,000 for 5 years. The cost of capital is 8% (cumulative discount factor 3.993). Calculate the NPV and the percentage by which the initial investment could rise before the project ceases to be worthwhile.
items.answer: NPV $25,363; sensitivity 7.5%
items.markingKey: PV of inflows $91,000 × 3.993 = $363,363 [1]; NPV $25,363 [1]; sensitivity of initial investment = $25,363 / $338,000 × 100 = 7.5% [1]
